---
title: "7. Artifact Registry and GKE"
description: "Store the Lemonade image in Artifact Registry, understand tags versus digests, and see how the k3s skills from Part 2 carry over to GKE Autopilot."
---

Cloud Run and GKE both pull images from a registry. On Google Cloud, that registry is **Artifact Registry**. This lesson stores the Lemonade image there, then shows what changes, and what stays the same, when you run the Part 2 manifests on Google's managed Kubernetes.

## The problem

1. CI builds `lemonade-stand` on every commit. The image needs a private home **in London**, next to Cloud Run, so deploys are fast and nobody outside can download it.
2. One day the shop may need more than Cloud Run offers, such as background workers, a queue and a database in one cluster. The owner already knows k3s from Part 2. Must they learn everything again?

## Explain it like I'm ten

::: {.callout-tip}
**Artifact Registry** is a **library for lunchboxes**. Each lunchbox is a container image.

- A **tag** is a **sticker** on the lunchbox, such as `v1`. Stickers can be peeled off and stuck on a different box.
- A **digest** is the box's **fingerprint**. It is calculated from what is inside, so it can never move to another box.
- Lunchboxes are packed in **layers**: bread, filling, fruit. If ten lunchboxes use the same bread, the library keeps **one** loaf.

**GKE Autopilot** is like a **hotel** instead of a house. With k3s you own the house: you fix the plumbing and buy new beds. With Autopilot you only **book rooms** (pods), say how big each room must be (resource requests), and the hotel builds and cleans the floors (nodes) for you.

Google ran its own services in containers on a system called **Borg** for about a decade before it open-sourced Kubernetes in 2014. The Borg paper by Abhishek Verma and colleagues ([EuroSys 2015](https://research.google/pubs/pub43438/)) explains the ideas Kubernetes, and therefore GKE, grew from: declare what you want and let the system pack the work onto machines.
:::

## The idea, precisely

### Repositories and image names

An Artifact Registry Docker repository lives in one location. A full image reference has five parts:

```text
europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev / lemonade-stand-dev / lemonade / lemonade-stand : v1
└──── registry host ───────┘  └── project ID ───┘  └ repo ─┘  └── image ────┘   └ tag
```

| Part | Lemonade value | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host | `europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev` | `<location>-docker.pkg.dev` |
| Project | `lemonade-stand-dev` | the project ID |
| Repository | `lemonade` | created once with `gcloud artifacts repositories create` |
| Image | `lemonade-stand` | the app name |
| Tag or digest | `:v1` or `@sha256:…` | tags can move; digests cannot |

The older Container Registry (`gcr.io`) is deprecated; new work uses Artifact Registry.

### Tags and digests

A **digest** is the SHA-256 hash of the image manifest. Change one byte of the image and the digest changes completely. A **tag** is just a name that points at a digest, and `docker push` can move it. So "v1 yesterday" and "v1 today" might be different images, but `@sha256:…` always means the same bytes.

### Access

- `roles/artifactregistry.reader`: may pull. Give it to the Cloud Run or GKE service account.
- `roles/artifactregistry.writer`: may push. Give it to the CI service account.
- `gcloud auth configure-docker europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev` teaches your local Docker to log in with your gcloud credentials.

### GKE Autopilot in one page

GKE is Google's managed Kubernetes. In **Autopilot** mode, Google also runs the nodes: you deploy pods, and GKE creates, sizes, patches and removes the machines underneath. You pay for the **CPU and memory your pods request**, plus a small hourly cluster fee.

Everything from Part 2 that talks to the Kubernetes API works unchanged: `kubectl`, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Jobs, probes and resource requests. What changes is the plumbing that k3s bundled:

| In k3s (Part 2) | In GKE Autopilot | What you do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| k3s server (control plane) | run by Google | nothing |
| k3s agents (nodes) | created automatically from pod requests | always set `resources.requests` |
| Flannel networking | GKE Dataplane V2 | nothing |
| Traefik Ingress | GKE Ingress (Google Cloud load balancer) or Gateway API | replace Traefik-specific settings |
| ServiceLB for `type: LoadBalancer` | a Google Cloud network load balancer | nothing: you get a real external IP |
| local-path provisioner | Persistent Disk CSI, StorageClass `standard-rwo` | change `storageClassName`, or omit it |
| `/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml` | `gcloud container clusters get-credentials` | one command |

## Command reference

| Command or flag | What it does | Rule / convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gcloud artifacts repositories create` | creates a repository | same region as Cloud Run | `gcloud artifacts repositories create lemonade --repository-format=docker --location=europe-west2` |
| `--description` | a human note | | `--description="Lemonade images"` |
| `gcloud auth configure-docker` | lets Docker push and pull with gcloud credentials | once per host name | `gcloud auth configure-docker europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev` |
| `docker push` | uploads an image | tag with the full reference first | `docker push europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade/lemonade-stand:v1` |
| `gcloud artifacts docker images list` | lists images and digests | | `gcloud artifacts docker images list europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade` |
| `gcloud artifacts docker tags list` | shows which digest each tag points at | | `gcloud artifacts docker tags list europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade/lemonade-stand` |
| `gcloud artifacts docker images delete` | deletes an image | add `--delete-tags` | `gcloud artifacts docker images delete …/lemonade-stand:old --delete-tags` |
| `gcloud artifacts repositories set-cleanup-policies` | deletes old images automatically | dry-run a policy first | `… set-cleanup-policies lemonade --location=europe-west2 --policy=cleanup.json` |
| `gcloud builds submit` | builds an image in Cloud Build, with no local Docker | | `gcloud builds submit --tag=europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade/lemonade-stand:v1` |
| `gcloud container clusters create-auto` | creates an Autopilot cluster | regional by design | `gcloud container clusters create-auto lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2` |
| `gcloud container clusters get-credentials` | writes a kubectl context | then use `kubectl` as in Part 2 | `gcloud container clusters get-credentials lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2` |
| `gcloud container clusters list` / `delete` | lists or removes clusters | delete when done: the fee runs hourly | `gcloud container clusters delete lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2` |

## Worked example: push once, run anywhere

```bash
REGISTRY=europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade

gcloud artifacts repositories create lemonade --repository-format=docker --location=europe-west2
gcloud auth configure-docker europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev

docker build --platform=linux/amd64 -t "$REGISTRY/lemonade-stand:v1" ../ci-cd/examples/lemonade-stand
docker push "$REGISTRY/lemonade-stand:v1"
```

Illustrative output of the push and the tag list:

```text
v1: digest: sha256:4c1e0b9f2d7a…e83a size: 1573

$ gcloud artifacts docker tags list $REGISTRY/lemonade-stand
TAG  IMAGE                                                                       DIGEST
v1   europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev/lemonade-stand-dev/lemonade/lemonade-stand      sha256:4c1e0b9f2d7a…e83a
```

The same image now runs in both places:

```bash
# Cloud Run (lesson 6)
gcloud run deploy lemonade-web --image="$REGISTRY/lemonade-stand:v1" --region=europe-west2

# GKE Autopilot, reusing the Part 2 manifests
gcloud container clusters create-auto lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2
gcloud container clusters get-credentials lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2
kubectl set image deployment/lemonade-web -n lemonade web="$REGISTRY/lemonade-stand:v1"
```

The last line assumes the Deployment from [Part 2](../k3s/index.qmd) is already applied with `kubectl apply`, and that its container is named `web`. Everything you learned there works on this cluster.

## Rules and conventions

- One repository per application, or per team, in the **same region** as the services that pull from it.
- CI pushes images tagged with the **Git commit SHA** (`lemonade-stand:3f9c2ab`). Humans may add friendly tags such as `v1.2.0`.
- Production deploys pin the **digest** (`@sha256:…`) or an immutable SHA tag, so a moved tag cannot change what runs.
- Grant `artifactregistry.writer` only to CI, and `artifactregistry.reader` to runtimes.
- Add a **cleanup policy** so old images do not pile up on the bill forever.
- On Autopilot, always set CPU and memory **requests**: they are both the bill and the scheduling input.
- Pick GKE only when you need Kubernetes features. For one stateless web app, Cloud Run is simpler and cheaper.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skipping `configure-docker` | `denied: Unauthenticated request` on `docker push` | `gcloud auth configure-docker europe-west2-docker.pkg.dev` |
| Pushing to a repository that does not exist | `name unknown: Repository "lemonade" not found` | create it first |
| Wrong host name, such as `europe-west2.pkg.dev` | `no such host` | the host is `<location>-docker.pkg.dev` |
| Deploying `:latest` | a rollback brings back the "wrong" latest | deploy a SHA tag or a digest |
| No resource requests on Autopilot | pods get Autopilot's default size and the bill is higher than expected | set `resources.requests` on every container |
| Keeping the Traefik-only parts of a k3s Ingress | the Ingress gets no address on GKE | use GKE Ingress or the Gateway API |
| Forgetting the test cluster | a fee every hour, every day | `gcloud container clusters delete lemonade-auto --region=europe-west2` |

## Mathematical Abstraction

**A digest is a hash of the content.**

$$
d = H(m)
$$

where:

- $m$ is the image manifest, the small JSON file that lists the image's layers;
- $H$ is SHA-256, a function that turns any input into a 64-hex-digit fingerprint;
- $d$ is the digest, written `sha256:<64 hex digits>`.

Example (real output of `printf '…' | shasum -a 256` on two tiny inputs):

- $H(\texttt{"lemonade v1"}) = \texttt{c8c38131…add94d27e}$
- $H(\texttt{"lemonade v2"}) = \texttt{b02aa2a9…ba222f491}$

One character changed, and the fingerprint changed completely. That is why a digest can never point at the wrong image, while a tag is only a movable label $\tau(\texttt{v1}) = d$ that a new push can repoint.

**Shared layers are stored once.** A registry keeps each layer once per repository, keyed by its digest.

$$
S = \sum_{\ell \,\in\, L_1 \cup L_2 \cup \cdots \cup L_k} \operatorname{size}(\ell)
$$

where:

- $k$ is the number of image versions in the repository;
- $L_i$ is the set of layers in version $i$;
- $L_1 \cup \cdots \cup L_k$ is the set of **distinct** layers, so a shared layer is counted only once;
- $\operatorname{size}(\ell)$ is the compressed size of layer $\ell$ in MB;
- $S$ is the storage used.

Example: every Lemonade version shares the same Node.js base layers, about 50 MB in total, plus its own app layer of about 2 MB. With $k = 10$ versions, the distinct layers are the base (50 MB) and ten app layers ($10 \times 2 = 20$ MB), so $S = 50 + 20 = 70$ MB. Counting each image separately would give $10 \times 52 = 520$ MB. This idealised model assumes the base layers really are identical. Upgrading the base image adds a new 50 MB set.

**On Autopilot you pay for what pods request.**

$$
R_{\text{cpu}} = \sum_{p \in P} r_{\text{cpu}}(p), \qquad R_{\text{mem}} = \sum_{p \in P} r_{\text{mem}}(p)
$$

where:

- $P$ is the set of running pods;
- $r_{\text{cpu}}(p)$ is pod $p$'s CPU request in vCPU (`250m` = $0.25$), and $r_{\text{mem}}(p)$ its memory request in GiB;
- $R_{\text{cpu}}$ and $R_{\text{mem}}$ are the totals that GKE bills per hour, at its per-vCPU and per-GiB rates.

Example: the Lemonade Deployment runs 3 replicas, each requesting `250m` CPU and `512Mi` memory. Then $R_{\text{cpu}} = 3 \times 0.25 = 0.75$ vCPU and $R_{\text{mem}} = 3 \times 0.5 = 1.5$ GiB. Over a 730-hour month, that is $0.75 \times 730 = 547.5$ vCPU-hours and $1.5 \times 730 = 1095$ GiB-hours, whatever size the hidden nodes are. Doubling the replicas to 6 doubles both numbers. On k3s on your own VM, by contrast, you pay for the whole VM even when it is half empty.
